mainTopic: The ארבע כוסות at the סדר: how much wine each cup needs, cases of drinking them in an unusual way, what the wine must be like, and who is obligated to drink them.
overview: This amud opens by finishing a statement from the previous amud: women are obligated in the ארבע כוסות because they too were part of the miracle of יציאת מצרים. Then רב יהודה quotes שמואל, who sets a minimum amount of wine for each cup. שמואל also lists three cases that still count: drinking the wine undiluted, drinking all four at once, and sharing the cups with one's household. The גמרא goes through each case and limits it. Undiluted wine misses the 'freedom' part (רבא). Drinking all at once does not count as four cups (רב). Sharing works only if he drank most of the cup (רב נחמן בר יצחק). Next, a ברייתא requiring a רביעית per cup seems to contradict שמואל's measure, and the גמרא shows that both describe the same amount. רבא gives the פסוק behind רבי יהודה's view that the wine must look like wine. Finally, a ברייתא teaches that men, women, and children are all obligated. רבי יהודה questions giving wine to children, and his alternative continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Women were also part of the miracle
steps.stepSummary: This line finishes a statement on the previous amud. Women are obligated in the ארבע כוסות because they too were saved in the miracle of יציאת מצרים.
steps.simpleTranslation: Because they too were included in that miracle.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing a statement that began on the previous amud: women must drink the ארבע כוסות. This line gives the reason.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally women are exempt from a מצות עשה שהזמן גרמא, a positive commandment tied to a specific time. Here the reason given is that the women were saved too, so they share in celebrating the miracle. That is why they are obligated even though the מצוה is tied to a time.

keyTerms.meaning: Miracle (here, the miracle of יציאת מצרים)
The four cups of wine drunk at the סדר

steps.confusionAlert: This line is not a new idea. It is the second half of a sentence from the previous section, which says women are obligated in the four cups.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is the classic source for why women are fully obligated in the ארבע כוסות and the other מצוות of the סדר night.

phrases.english: For they too were included in that miracle.
phrases.notes: 'They' means the women. This finishes the previous statement that women are obligated in the four cups.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the reason for a ruling stated on the previous amud (women are obligated in the four cups).
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Women are obligated in the four cups because they too were saved in the miracle.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The miracle covered everyone, so everyone celebrates it.

steps.title: How much wine each cup must hold
steps.stepSummary: שמואל, quoted by רב יהודה, says each of the four cups must have enough wine to make one proper, full-sized mixed cup.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה said in the name of שמואל: These four cups must each contain enough wine to make a proper diluted cup.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new statement from שמואל. It sets the minimum amount of wine for each of the four cups.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the time of the גמרא, wine was very strong and people mixed it with water before drinking. שמואל says each cup needs enough wine that, once it is mixed, it makes a respectable cup, not just a few drops. The four cups are a real measured obligation, not just a symbolic sip.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets the size requirement for each cup. The גמרא itself (Step 8) shows it is the same as the ברייתא's measure of a רביעית.

phrases.english: Rav Yehuda said that Shmuel said:
phrases.notes: רב יהודה is passing on what his teacher שמואל taught.

phrases.english: These four cups
phrases.notes: The four cups of the סדר.

phrases.english: must have in them
enough for mixing a proper cup.
phrases.notes: Enough wine that, once water is added, it makes a full, respectable cup.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic: the details of how the four cups are drunk.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Each of the four cups must contain enough wine to make a proper diluted cup.

steps.title: Three ways that still count
steps.stepSummary: שמואל continues with three cases where a person still fulfills the obligation: drinking the wine undiluted, drinking all four cups at once, or giving the cups to his children and household to drink.
steps.simpleTranslation: If he drank them undiluted, he fulfilled his obligation. If he drank them all at once, he fulfilled it. If he gave his children and household members to drink from them, he fulfilled it.
steps.whatsHappening: שמואל lists three less-than-ideal ways of drinking the four cups and says each one still counts. This list sets up the next three steps, where the גמרא comments on each case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each case changes one detail of the normal practice. The wine is not mixed with water, or the four separate cups are merged into one drink, or the person does not drink all of it himself. שמואל's rule is that none of these changes cancels the מצוה completely. The coming steps will add limits to these rulings.

keyTerms.meaning: All at once, in a single drink

steps.confusionAlert: 'יצא' here does not mean this is the right way to do it. It only means that after the fact, the obligation was not totally lost. The next steps will show that some of these cases are only partly fulfilled.

phrases.english: If he drank them undiluted, he fulfilled his obligation.
If he drank them all at once, he fulfilled his obligation.
phrases.notes: Case 2: all four cups' worth of wine drunk in one go.

phrases.aramaic: הִשְׁקָה מֵהֶן לְבָנָיו וְלִבְנֵי בֵיתוֹ — יָצָא.
phrases.english: If he gave his sons and household members to drink from them, he fulfilled his obligation.
phrases.notes: Case 3: he shared the cups with others.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues שמואל's same statement and moves from the amount of wine to cases where the cups were drunk in an unusual way.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Drinking undiluted, drinking all at once, or sharing with one's household still counts as fulfilling the obligation.

steps.title: Undiluted wine counts only partly
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא returns to שמואל's first case. רבא explains that drinking undiluted wine fulfills the obligation to drink wine, but not the obligation to drink in a way that shows freedom.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'If he drank them undiluted, he fulfilled his obligation': רבא said, he fulfilled the obligation of wine, but he did not fulfill the obligation of freedom.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes שמואל's first case again, and רבא narrows it. The person only partly fulfilled his obligation.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא splits the מצוה into two parts. One part is the drinking of wine, and that was done. The other part is drinking like a free, noble person, and that was not done, because refined people did not drink harsh, unmixed wine. So שמואל's 'יצא' only means the wine part was fulfilled.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows that the four cups are not only about drinking wine. They are meant to be drunk the way free people drink, which is the theme of the whole סדר.

phrases.english: 'If he drank them undiluted, he fulfilled his obligation':
phrases.notes: The גמרא quotes שמואל's first case again in order to comment on it.

phrases.english: Rava said: he fulfilled the obligation of wine,
but he did not fulfill the obligation of freedom.
phrases.notes: Drinking strong unmixed wine is not how free, refined people drink.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Narrows the first of שמואל's three cases.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Undiluted wine fulfills the wine part but not the freedom part of the מצוה.

steps.title: Drinking all at once is not four cups
steps.stepSummary: On שמואל's second case, רב says that drinking all four at once fulfills the obligation of drinking wine, but not the obligation of four separate cups.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'If he drank them all at once': רב said, he fulfilled the obligation of wine, but he did not fulfill the obligation of four cups.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא turns to the second case. רב holds that drinking all the wine in one gulp does not count as the four cups.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Like רבא in the previous step, רב divides the obligation into parts. Drinking wine for the joy of the יום טוב was done. But the מצוה is four separate cups, each drunk at its own point in the סדר, and that was not done. On this case רב disagrees with שמואל's plain 'יצא': for רב, the four-cups obligation itself was not fulfilled.

phrases.english: 'If he drank them all at once':
Rav said: he fulfilled the obligation of wine,
phrases.notes: He drank wine for the joy of the יום טוב.

phrases.english: but he did not fulfill the obligation of four cups.
phrases.notes: Four cups means four separate drinkings.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the same 'wine vs. something more' split as רבא, now applied to the second case.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Drinking all four at once fulfills the wine obligation but not the four-cups obligation.

steps.title: Sharing counts only if he drank most
steps.stepSummary: On שמואל's third case, רב נחמן בר יצחק adds a condition: sharing the cups with family only works if he himself drank most of each cup.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'If he gave his sons and household members to drink from them, he fulfilled his obligation': רב נחמן בר יצחק said, and this is only when he himself drank most of the cup.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the third case again, and רב נחמן בר יצחק adds a requirement to it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Sharing is allowed, but the person still has to do the drinking himself. He must drink most of the cup, called רובא דכסא. Letting his family drink most of it would mean he did not really drink the cup at all.

keyTerms.meaning: And this is only when (introduces a condition)

steps.whatToRemember: שמואל gave three cases that 'count'. Each one was then limited. Undiluted wine misses the freedom part (רבא). Drinking all at once misses the four-cups part (רב). Sharing works only if he drank most of the cup (רב נחמן בר יצחק).
steps.whyThisMatters: This is the source for the practice of drinking most of each cup at the סדר.

phrases.aramaic: הִשְׁקָה מֵהֶן לְבָנָיו וְלִבְנֵי בֵיתוֹ — יָצָא,
phrases.english: 'If he gave his sons and household members to drink from them, he fulfilled his obligation':
Rav Nachman bar Yitzchak said:
And this is only when he drank most of the cup.
phrases.notes: The person himself must drink most of each cup.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב נַחְמָן בַּר יִצְחָק: וְהוּא דְּאִשְׁתִּי רוּבָּא דְכָסָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes going through שמואל's three cases by limiting the last one.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Sharing the cups works only if he drank most of each cup himself.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Each of שמואל's lenient cases has a limit.

steps.title: A ברייתא seems to give a different measure for the cups
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes a ברייתא requiring each cup to hold a רביעית. This seems to contradict שמואל's measure of 'enough to mix a good cup.'
steps.simpleTranslation: They challenged this from a ברייתא: These four cups must each hold a רביעית. It does not matter if the wine is undiluted or diluted, new or aged. רבי יהודה says the wine must have the taste and look of wine. The ברייתא says 'a רביעית,' but you (שמואל) said 'a good cup'!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that seems to give a different size for the cups than שמואל gave in Step 2. It uses this to challenge שמואל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: שמואל described the amount as 'enough to mix one good cup.' The ברייתא uses a different measure: a רביעית for each cup. The challenge is that these look like two different amounts, so שמואל seems to disagree with a ברייתא.

keyTerms.meaning: A quarter-לוג, the standard size of a cup
'In any case, it teaches': points to the part of a source that matters for the challenge

steps.confusionAlert: Don't think רבי יהודה's line is part of the challenge. The challenge comes only from the first part, which says each cup needs a רביעית. רבי יהודה's line will be explained later, in Step 9.

phrases.english: They challenged: These four cups
phrases.notes: Here the גמרא starts quoting a ברייתא.

phrases.english: must contain the amount of a quarter-log,
whether undiluted or diluted,
whether new or aged.

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר: צָרִיךְ שֶׁיְּהֵא בּוֹ
phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda says: it must have in it
the taste and appearance of wine.
In any case, it teaches 'the amount of a quarter-log,'
and you said 'a good cup'!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Goes back to שמואל's measure from Step 2 and challenges it with a ברייתא.
steps.kashyaTarget: שמואל's measure: 'enough to mix one good cup'
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא requires a רביעית per cup. שמואל's wording suggests a different amount, so שמואל seems to contradict the ברייתא.

steps.title: Both measures are really the same amount
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that שמואל and the ברייתא are giving the same measure, just described in different ways.
steps.simpleTranslation: They answer: Both are one measure. What did שמואל mean by 'enough to mix a good cup'? He meant enough pure wine for each cup to become a full cup once water is added. All four cups together then hold a רביעית of pure wine.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge by showing that שמואל and the ברייתא agree.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Wine was mixed with about three parts water. A full cup (a רביעית) therefore needed only a quarter-רביעית of pure wine. שמואל was describing the pure wine in each cup, so all four cups together contain one רביעית of pure wine. The ברייתא was describing the full, mixed cup, which is a רביעית each. So there is no disagreement.

keyTerms.meaning: 'This and that': both sources are saying the same thing

steps.whatToRemember: Each cup needs a full רביעית once mixed. That works out to a quarter-רביעית of pure wine per cup, or one רביעית of pure wine across all four cups.

phrases.aramaic: אָמְרִי: אִידֵּי וְאִידֵּי חַד שִׁיעוּרָא הוּא,
phrases.english: They say: this and that are one measure,
what is 'enough to mix a good cup' that he said?
for each and every one of the cups,
so that all of them together come to a quarter-log.
phrases.notes: Each cup needs only a quarter of a רביעית of pure wine, and four of those add up to one רביעית.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמְרִי: אִידֵּי וְאִידֵּי חַד שִׁיעוּרָא הוּא
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reinterpretation: both sources describe the same amount in different terms
steps.terutzHavaAmina: שמואל's 'good cup' seemed to be a different amount from the ברייתא's רביעית.
steps.terutzMaskana: שמואל describes the pure wine per cup, which totals one רביעית over four cups. The ברייתא describes the mixed cup, which is a רביעית each. They are the same measure.

steps.title: רבא gives the verse behind רבי יהודה's view
steps.stepSummary: רבא explains that רבי יהודה requires the wine to look like wine because of the פסוק 'Do not look at wine when it is red.'
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהודה says the wine must have taste and appearance. רבא said: What is רבי יהודה's reason? Because it is written: 'Do not look at wine when it turns red.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא returns to רבי יהודה's line from the ברייתא. רבא gives the source for why the wine's look matters.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Taste is obviously important for wine. Why should appearance matter too? The פסוק describes wine by its red color, which shows that the look of wine is part of what makes it wine. So a cup watered down until it no longer looks red would not count for רבי יהודה.

keyTerms.meaning: 'What is the reason?': asks for the source of a view

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר: צָרִיךְ שֶׁיְּהֵא בּוֹ טַעַם וּמַרְאֶה.
phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda says: it must have taste and appearance.
phrases.notes: The גמרא quotes the ברייתא again so it can explain it.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רָבָא: מַאי טַעְמָא דְּרַבִּי יְהוּדָה,
phrases.english: Rava said: What is the reason of Rabbi Yehuda?
As it is written: 'Do not look at wine when it is red' (Proverbs 23:31).

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רָבָא: מַאי טַעְמָא דְּרַבִּי יְהוּדָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the measure question and explains the second part of the ברייתא from Step 7.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רבי יהודה, the wine must look like wine (red), based on the פסוק 'אל תרא יין כי יתאדם'.

steps.title: Everyone is obligated in the four cups
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא teaches that men, women, and children are all obligated to drink the ארבע כוסות.
steps.simpleTranslation: The רבנן taught: Everyone is obligated in these four cups: men, women, and children.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new ברייתא about who must drink the four cups.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This adds a new piece of information: the obligation is not limited to adult men. Women and even children are included, which sets up רבי יהודה's question about children in the next step.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is a source for women being fully obligated in the ארבע כוסות, and for including children in the סדר.

phrases.english: The Rabbis taught: all are obligated
in these four cups,

phrases.aramaic: אֶחָד אֲנָשִׁים, וְאֶחָד נָשִׁים, וְאֶחָד תִּינוֹקוֹת.
phrases.english: men, women, and children alike.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: הַכֹּל חַיָּיבִין בְּאַרְבָּעָה כּוֹסוֹת הַלָּלוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on to a new topic: who is obligated in the cups.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Men, women, and children are all obligated in the ארבע כוסות.

steps.title: רבי יהודה questions why children need wine
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה asks what benefit children get from wine and begins to say what should be given to them instead. The sentence continues on the next amud.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהודה said: What benefit do children get from wine? Rather, we hand out to them...
steps.whatsHappening: Inside the same ברייתא, רבי יהודה disagrees about children. His suggestion of what to give them continues in the next section.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The point of the cups is enjoyment and a feeling of freedom, and children do not really enjoy wine. So רבי יהודה says giving them wine misses the purpose. He starts to suggest giving them something they do enjoy instead.
steps.confusionAlert: The sentence is cut off here. 'We hand out to them' is finished on the next amud, which says what is given to the children.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבִּי יְהוּדָה: וְכִי מָה תּוֹעֶלֶת
phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda said: But what benefit
do children have from wine?
Rather, we distribute to them
phrases.notes: The sentence carries on to the next amud.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יְהוּדָה: וְכִי מָה תּוֹעֶלֶת יֵשׁ לְתִינוֹקוֹת בְּיַיִן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: רבי יהודה disagrees with the ברייתא's inclusion of children from Step 10.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רבי יהודה, children are not given wine, since they get no benefit from it. Instead they receive something else, which is explained on the next amud.
